N01: For Union goods, establish free-circulation status at the designated customs post before choosing Annex 19. A mixed Union/non-Union operation follows the separate Annex 21 route described by Customs; an Annex 19 authorisation alone does not establish that route. Regulation 3 of LN 2026/211 defines Union goods and indirect tax; regulation 4 applies the listed Union rules with the domestic replacements in Schedule 2. [LN 2026/211, regulations 3–4 and Schedules 1–2](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/legislations/tgeu-implementation-special-customs-procedures-concerning-union-goods-regulations-2026-8575/download); [Annex 19 guidance, introduction](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/uploads/_PressOffice/Treaty%20Customs%20Guidance/Annex%2019%20Special%20Customs%20Procedures%20GN%20FINAL.pdf).
N02: For Union-goods special procedures, first follow the OFT trading-licence process. After its formalities and before the licence is granted, apply to HM Customs Gibraltar for the procedure authorisation; OFT issues the licence after that authorisation. Warehousing/inward-processing preparation includes a premises plan and relevant segregation, traceable digital inventory, security, Customs access and a guarantee covering tax/duty. Temporary admission requires unaltered goods and a guarantee. Existing operators continuing after the transition keep the existing licence under the specific guidance exception, but still need the new procedure authorisation. These are published requirements, not approval of any actual premises or guarantee. [Guidance, sections 2–3 and 5.3–5.4](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/uploads/_PressOffice/Treaty%20Customs%20Guidance/Annex%2019%20Special%20Customs%20Procedures%20GN%20FINAL.pdf).
N03: For authorised Union-goods warehousing, the T2GI ends when the Gibraltar IM7 clears; move the goods to the approved warehouse. Discharge through IM4 home use or the appropriate EX3 re-export, IM5 “5001” inward processing or IM9 destruction route. Warehousing permits storage and the specified usual handling such as packing, cleaning or refrigeration; further processing needs inward processing. Regulation 4(3) says the non-ship-supplies period is “between one month and nine months”; guidance 1.1.4 says it must exceed one month and be less than nine months. Do not decide an exact one- or nine-month boundary from the guidance alone. Ship supplies have no minimum. [LN 2026/188, regulation 4(3)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/legislations/tgeu-implementation-annex-19-regulations-2026-8553/download); [guidance 1.1](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/uploads/_PressOffice/Treaty%20Customs%20Guidance/Annex%2019%20Special%20Customs%20Procedures%20GN%20FINAL.pdf).
N04: For Union-goods inward processing, close the T2GI using IM5 extended code “5001”, use the approved premises, and discharge both processed products and waste through the proper IM4, EX3, IM7 or IM9 route. Goods can instead be released for home use or re-exported unchanged. Temporary admission uses IM5, the declared use and an EX3 to close on re-export. Both have an ordinary three-month limit. A longer initial period or extension requires duly justified circumstances accepted by the designated post which opened the T2GI under regulation 4(6); an operator cannot grant its own extension. [Guidance 1.2–1.3](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/uploads/_PressOffice/Treaty%20Customs%20Guidance/Annex%2019%20Special%20Customs%20Procedures%20GN%20FINAL.pdf); [LN 2026/188, regulation 4(3), (6)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/legislations/tgeu-implementation-annex-19-regulations-2026-8553/download).
N05: Keep the authorisation, arrival/clearance, inventory movements, removal declaration, tax/excise payments and discharge evidence together. Customs must send arrival advice on the presentation day and control results within three working days; a special-procedure message replaces proof of tax at that stage. Customs supplies case-by-case exit/destruction evidence or monthly tax proof for market releases. These are authority-to-authority reporting duties, not an extra three-day filing allowance for a trader. Missing proofs or failure to discharge can trigger the transfer of Member State VAT/excise under regulation 4(7). [LN 2026/188, regulation 4(2)–(7)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/legislations/tgeu-implementation-annex-19-regulations-2026-8553/download); [guidance section 4](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/uploads/_PressOffice/Treaty%20Customs%20Guidance/Annex%2019%20Special%20Customs%20Procedures%20GN%20FINAL.pdf).
N06: The retained Imports and Exports Act requires an import entry within the relevant period, subject to sections 24 and 26: section 17 states seven clear days for air and fourteen clear days otherwise, using its defined report/arrival date and infectious-disease restriction proviso. Section 23 permits transit-shed deposit or sale of perishable goods on the specified failures, including the separate 21-clear-day clearance limb. These are residual entry rules. Section 2A and TGEU Schedule 1 paragraphs 12–14 make the Act subordinate to the treaty and disapply the old import-duty charge. They do not override immediate presentation, special transit or payment-before-release requirements. [Imports and Exports Act, sections 2A, 17, 21–23](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/legislations/imports-and-exports-act-1986-423/download); [TGEU Act, Schedule 1 paragraphs 12–14](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf); [Transit guidance section 2](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/uploads/_PressOffice/Treaty%20Customs%20Guidance/Transit%20GN.pdf).
N07: Within the Union-goods special-procedure regime, Schedule 2 Part A replacements for UCC Articles 102 and 108 require the notified debt to be paid within the Customs-prescribed period, no longer than ten days after notification, subject to the listed suspension cases. Release itself counts as notification where the declared amount equals the payable amount; a guaranteed aggregate notification period cannot exceed 30 days. Deferment under replacements 110–111 needs an application and Customs authorisation, with a guarantee if required, for at most 30 days beginning the day after notification. Other payment facilities under replacement 112 require a guarantee. This bounded regime does not confer a general ten- or thirty-day grace period on an ordinary IM4 release. [LN 2026/211, Schedule 2 Part A paragraphs 31, 37–41](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/legislations/tgeu-implementation-special-customs-procedures-concerning-union-goods-regulations-2026-8575/download).
N08: For a debt within that Union-goods special-procedure regime, identify the repayment/remission ground first: overcharge, defective/non-contract goods, Customs error or equity, or invalidated declaration. Replacement 116 normally uses a £10 threshold but permits a requested lower repayment. Replacement 121 gives three years from notification for its overcharge/error/equity limb, one year for defective/non-contract goods, and the applicable invalidation period for invalidated declarations. Evidence of unforeseeable circumstances or force majeure extends the first two periods; an Article 44 appeal suspends their running while it is pending. The applicant submits to HM Customs Gibraltar. These are not a verified deadline or form for the separate section 102 commercial-export refund. [LN 2026/211, regulation 3 and Schedule 2 Part A paragraphs 45–50](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/legislations/tgeu-implementation-special-customs-procedures-concerning-union-goods-regulations-2026-8575/download).
N09: For that special-procedure regime, non-compliance with movement, storage, processing, temporary-admission or reduced-rate conditions can itself create an indirect-tax customs debt; responsible persons and knowing participants/holders can be liable under replacement 79. Overdue debt is enforceable and replacement 114 charges interest from expiry of the prescribed payment period until payment, without stating a numerical interest rate. Do not substitute a UK/EU interest percentage. [LN 2026/211, Schedule 2 Part A paragraphs 8, 42–43](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/legislations/tgeu-implementation-special-customs-procedures-concerning-union-goods-regulations-2026-8575/download).
N10: Failure to make a required entry under section 21 is punishable on summary conviction by a level 3 standard-scale fine. Section 109 covers materially untrue import/export documents or statements for goods whether dutiable or not; its knowing/reckless offence carries up to six months and a level 4 fine on summary conviction, or two years and twice level 5 on indictment. Section 117 supplies a level 4 summary fine where the Act gives no specific penalty. These are the retained customs offences subject to treaty primacy, not a newly verified universal transaction-tax penalty or a conversion of scale levels to pounds. [Imports and Exports Act, sections 2A, 21(3), 109, 117](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/legislations/imports-and-exports-act-1986-423/download).
N11: For a warehouse re-export, Customs guidance 4.1 requires EX3 before removal, the original import MRN and the correct NCTS T1GI/T2GI movement, followed by EPU export clearance and the Spanish designated-post arrival/closure. Its Spanish Entry Summary Declaration instruction is one hour before arrival. Distinguish this warehouse re-export from the tax-paid EX1 route above. Preserve destination tax and discharge records; neither code alone proves a section 102 refund entitlement. [Goods Transit Process, section 4.1](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/uploads/_PressOffice/Treaty%20Customs%20Guidance/Transit%20GN.pdf).
N12: The aid-law chain is now identified: TGEU Act section 68(4) gives Annex 18 acts domestic force; Annex 18 applies them with necessary adaptations for Gibraltar and lists Regulation (EU) 2023/2831 at 3.4. For an ordinary case within that Regulation, Article 3(2) sets a EUR 300,000 ceiling for a single undertaking over any three-year period. Article 3(3) uses the legal grant date, not payment date; Article 3(5) measures gross grant equivalent, not the face amount of a profit deduction. Keep the grant/equivalent and currency evidence; this Guide supplies no sterling conversion or automatic remaining allowance. [Act section 68(4)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf); [Annex 18, opening provisions and 3.4](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6a56149a9e63154454413620/MS_9.2026_Agreement_Gibraltar_UK_EU_EAEC_v2of2.pdf); [Regulation 2023/2831, Article 3](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/2831/oj/eng).
N13: Apply the single-undertaking test across direct and indirect majority voting, board appointment/removal, contractual/constitutional dominant influence and voting agreements under Article 2(2); separate company names do not reset the ceiling. Article 3(8)–(9) accounts for mergers, acquisitions and splits. Article 1 excludes the stated primary agricultural/fishery activities, certain processing/marketing cases, export-linked and domestic-preference aid; separated accounts/activities are required for its mixed-activity exception. Article 5 controls cumulation with other aid, including the same-cost intensity/amount limit. Do not apply EUR 300,000 mechanically to excluded sectors or substitute the separate services-of-general-economic-interest regime. [Regulation 2023/2831, Articles 1–3 and 5](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/2831/oj/eng); [Annex 18, 3.4](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6a56149a9e63154454413620/MS_9.2026_Agreement_Gibraltar_UK_EU_EAEC_v2of2.pdf).
N14: Before relying on the transitional deduction, obtain the Commissioner’s acceptance of eligibility, the gross grant equivalent, linked-enterprise aid history and permissible remaining headroom. The Regulation requires an ex-ante precisely calculable equivalent and verification before a new grant; its declaration safeguard applies until the central register covers three years. Rule 6 additionally requires the claimant’s three-year preceding-claim aid declaration. A numerical ceiling does not itself establish a grant, approved deduction or sufficient headroom. [Regulation 2023/2831, Articles 4(1), 6(4), 7(4)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/2831/oj/eng); [Deductions Rules, rule 6](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2026s338/2026s338.pdf).
